observations: Large blue steel-framed industrial radiator/cooler unit with a circular fan and coiled core on top, sitting on wooden pallets in an outdoor equipment yard.
Other heavy equipment (generators, compressors, engine blocks) visible in the background, suggesting a used-machinery dealer's lot.
Orange ratchet straps secure the unit to the pallets, indicating it is set up for transport, not in operation.
The word 'HANSEN' is hand-written in yellow marker on the frame (photo 1 and photo 2) — this looks like a handler's or lot marking, not a manufacturer's nameplate.
Surface rust, grime, and paint wear are visible on the frame and fins in all three photos.
No manufacturer nameplate, serial number, or model tag is visible in any photo.
A watermark 'DNL EQUIPMENT SALES' appears across all three photos, consistent with a resale listing, not proof of the item's specification.

identity.kind: industrial engine cooling radiator / charge-air cooler unit

claims.claim: Cooling radiator to match Detroit Series 60
claims.evidence: No nameplate, part number, or engine-fitment marking visible in any photo; 'HANSEN' marker text does not confirm Detroit Series 60 compatibility.

claims.claim: Fits other engines with turbo cooler etc.
claims.evidence: No dimensions, port layout, or fitment documentation shown in photos.
Photos show visible surface rust and dirt on the frame and fins, which is not clearly 'clean'; full claim text is incomplete.

risks.risk: Core/fin condition — leaks, blockages, or corrosion inside the cooling coil are not visible from outside.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the fin/core surface and a pressure or flow test clip.

risks.risk: Fan motor or blade condition and whether it spins/functions.
risks.proof: Video clip of the fan running, or close-up of motor nameplate.

risks.risk: Actual fitment to Detroit Series 60 or other named engines is unconfirmed.
risks.proof: Photo of a manufacturer's part/model plate matching OEM cross-reference, or a fitment chart.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unverified-fit radiator, not as a confirmed Series 60 match

risks.risk: Hidden structural damage (cracks, dents) on the underside or mounting points not shown.
risks.proof: Photos of underside and all mounting brackets.

risks.risk: True ownership/origin of the 'HANSEN' marking is unclear — could be a brand, a prior owner's tag, or unrelated.
risks.proof: Photo of any stamped or riveted nameplate on the unit.

proof_requests: Clear photo of any manufacturer nameplate, serial number, or part number on the radiator frame.
Close-up photos of the core fins showing condition (no bent fins, no leaks/stains).
Video of the fan motor running to confirm it operates.
Measurements (length, width, height, port sizes) to confirm fitment claims.
Photo of the underside and all mounting brackets.
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as a used industrial engine-cooling radiator/fan unit, but the Detroit Series 60 fitment claim and working condition are unverifiable from the photos, so it must be priced at worst case (unconfirmed fitment, untested function, visible surface corrosion) pending the listed proof.
